adr_title: Legacy canvas-YAML interop reconciled — the `view` authority row, one level too high
decision_statement: The canvas_yaml_interop shape IS the aDNA Canvas Standard's `view` authority row — for the canvases that are actually DERIVED. Canonical placement is metadata.frontmatter._reserved; the migration is mechanical and verified; propagation is OFFERED to Rosetta, never performed. As amended: `authority` and `production` are MACHINE-enforced as A-8 since v2.4.0 (Amendment 1), and the migration is NOT ONE RECIPE (Amendment 2) — a canvas is derived iff `source_yaml` is non-empty AND resolves, in which case it takes `authority: view` + `production: generated`; otherwise it is a primary artifact and takes NEITHER key.
context: ⛔ READ BEFORE SIGNING — this ADR has been amended TWICE since you last saw it, and the second amendment corrects the first. AMENDMENT 1: Decision 4 asserted canvas_std does not know the `authority` key and that LIP-0010 was 'assessed, not taken'. Gridline shipped A-8 on 2026-09-11 — canvas_std VALIDATES both keys and LIP-0010 is FINAL. Struck, together with its §Consequences twin, in the same pass so neither could be 'verified' by reference to the other. A1 then added a blanket `production: "generated"` row to the migration table, because A-8 is asymmetric (`authority` REQUIRES `production`). AMENDMENT 2 — ⛔ THAT ROW WAS WRONG FOR THE MAJORITY, and it was found by red-teaming our own recommendation, not by any new external input. The corpus is TWO POPULATIONS that neither this ADR nor A1 partitioned. Measured 2026-09-16 across ~/aDNA/*/what/lattices/examples/*.canvas (Archive excluded, live vaults, this node): 258 canvases across 63 vaults — 194 SOURCELESS, 63 sourced-and-the-source-RESOLVES, 1 bare. Uniform per vault: one `hello_world.canvas` (cites hello_world.lattice.yaml, which exists) plus three `template_*` canvases citing nothing — and no template_*.lattice.yaml exists anywhere in the workspace, verified by find rather than assumed. ⇒ ≈3:1 AGAINST the recipe as written. And `view` is WRONG on the 194, not merely incomplete: your own Plumbline P1 ruling settled this population — 'a standalone hand-authored canvas that IS the primary artifact is not diagrammatic context at all' — so the axis does not apply and OMISSION is the correct answer. `view` asserts that another channel owns the meaning; for these there is no other channel. PROVENANCE, stated fairly: the 2026-02 legacy tooling stamped `authority: view` on everything it emitted, sourced or not. This ADR inherited that as ground truth — and it SAW THE SYMPTOM AND MISREAD IT, reporting that 'sync fields were never populated… declared for 6 months without ever being enforced' where the truth was 'these are not views'. Rosetta verified PLACEMENT and BYTE-IDENTITY, which is exactly what we asked of them — not semantics, and not their miss. ⭐ The `production` row was the single most confident claim in the whole package, offered as 'right by the pattern's own definition'. It is the one that was wrong: confidence was doing the work a partition should have done. WHAT ALREADY SHIPPED is unchanged by all this: v8.11 fired the RELOCATION half onto 8 files, which read core [OK] and adna_native FAIL (A-2 ×2, A-6, A-8). NOTHING IS BROKEN TODAY — they declare no conformance_level, so they validate at core and pass — and Rosetta scoped the release to '8 files… NOT the fleet'.

consequences_positive.value: A 6-month-old unowned drift becomes a named, recipe-complete offer — and the relocation half has already shipped upstream and worked.
`view` survived the 2026-09-11 axis split unchanged — checked, not assumed — and remains correct for the 63 genuinely-derived canvases.
As amended TWICE, the recipe finally matches the corpus: derived canvases take view + generated; the 194 primary ones take neither key, which A-8 accepts (verified at adna_native, not assumed).

The partition test is executable rather than described: source_yaml non-empty AND resolves ⇒ derived; otherwise primary. A declared source that does not resolve is evidence of a stamp, not of derivation.
No canvas_std change. This ratifies a DESCRIPTION, not a validator; the firewall stays at diff 0.

consequences_negative.value: ⛔ Ratifying endorses REMOVING `authority: view` from ~194 fleet canvases that have carried it since 2026-02. It is a deletion of a false claim, not of information — but it is a visible change to files many vaults hold.
Until the field-shape half lands, the 8 shipped files remain core-valid and adna_native-invalid. A KNOWN state now, rather than an unmeasured one.
Canvas cannot land the fix — it depends on Rosetta's template channel. This converts the drift into an offer, not a completion.
An erratum is owed to a peer who acted in good faith on our recipe — and it is now a BIGGER erratum than 'add a production row'. That is a cost of signing late, and it is ours.
Repairing the 8 already-migrated files is THEIRS to decide; this vault writes into neither .adna/ (Rule 1) nor their tree (Rule 10).

alternatives.title: Sign with Amendment 1 only (the blanket `production` row)
alternatives.rejected_because: it would bless a recipe that stamps `production: generated` onto 194 canvases generated from nothing, on top of an `authority: view` that is false of them. This is the option Amendment 2 exists to prevent — and it is the option that was on the table yesterday.

alternatives.title: Keep `authority: view` on the primary canvases and add `production: hand_authored`
alternatives.rejected_because: legal under A-8's asymmetry, and it avoids churn — but it preserves the original error, asserting an owner that does not exist. Ruled against: omission is Plumbline P1's answer for this population.

alternatives.title: Deprecate the interop spec and regenerate all canvases from source
alternatives.rejected_because: throws away a working mapping and hundreds of hand-checked files — and for the 194 primary ones there IS no source to regenerate from. That is the whole finding.

alternatives.title: Teach canvas_std to read metadata._reserved as a fallback
alternatives.rejected_because: a firewall change (LIP territory) that would legitimize two canonical paths forever and weaken A-2 for every future document.

recommendation.rationale: RATIFY AS AMENDED (×2). The core reconciliation — the legacy IS the Standard's `view` row, at the wrong path — was right in August and Rosetta confirmed it independently. What was wrong was scope: the ADR treated one corpus where there are two populations. Both amendments correct descriptions, not code, and both preserve the originals struck rather than deleted. ⚠ If you would rather not ratify a document that changed twice in a day, DEFER is a clean answer — nothing is failing in the meantime.
key_factors: The core reconciliation is independently confirmed — Rosetta verified at the object before accepting.
The partition is measured (258 / 194 / 63) and re-derived at session open, not carried from a plan.
Both amendments correct descriptions; no code, no schema, no A-8 behaviour change.
Nothing is currently failing: the 8 shipped files pass at their declared level.
risks: ⛔ This ADR has now been wrong twice in two different ways. A third population may exist that neither pass found — the partition test is derivable, so it can be re-run, and it should be before the fleet migration.
Signing does not repair the 8 shipped files — that needs the (now larger) erratum to reach Rosetta first.
Endorsing removal of `authority` from ~194 fleet files is a visible change; Rosetta owns whether and when it happens.
next_actions: Flip status: accepted and fill the §7.7 block — noting the signature is on the text AS AMENDED TWICE.
Rewrite memo #20's erratum payload: it is now 'partition before migrating', not 'add a production row'.
Re-run the partition test before any fleet migration, rather than trusting these figures.
